juniper-street-bakery-2.text:
Per croissant, yes, the price increase covered the butter cost increase, with room to spare. Overall, though, croissants are bringing in less weekly profit than before, because volume fell.

**The per-unit math**

Hollis raised cultured butter from $142.20 to $167.80 per 36 lb case (suppliers/hollis-prices-2026-08.csv, suppliers/hollis-prices-2026-09.csv), a $0.71/lb increase.

In the sales data (sales/weekly-sales-2026-W30-to-W38.csv), butter croissant unit cost rose from $1.12 to $1.38 (+$0.26) starting the week of 2026-08-31, the same week the menu price moved from $4.25 to $4.75 (+$0.50, per menu/fall-2026-menu.md). So margin per butter croissant actually went **up**, from $3.13 to $3.37. Almond croissant shows the same pattern: cost rose $1.41→$1.66, price rose $4.95→$5.45, margin up from $3.54 to $3.79.

**But total croissant profit fell**

Weekly units sold dropped after the price change:
- Butter croissant: averaged 404/week (W30–W35) before the change, down to 333/week (W36–W38) after.
- Combined butter + almond: the weekly-operations-brief-2026-W37.md notes 488 croissants sold in W37, "still well under the 588 to 619 we sold every week before the price change."

That volume drop outweighs the fatter per-unit margin. Combined butter + almond gross margin averaged about $1,970/week before the change and about $1,702/week after, a decline of roughly $268/week (about 13.6%).

```visual
{"kind":"bar","labels":["W30","W31","W32","W33","W34","W35","W36","W37","W38"],"series":[{"name":"Croissant gross margin","values":[1919.83,1993.46,2018.24,1955.08,2018.65,1914.65,1705.03,1707.56,1694.07]}],"format":"currency","currency":"USD"}
```

**On "did I lose regulars"**

The data doesn't track repeat customers, so it can't confirm that directly. But customers/feedback-log.md has a 2026-09-03 Google review: "Croissant went up fifty cents and felt smaller" (3 stars), and two regulars on 2026-09-06 asked if the almond croissant was gone for good since it kept selling out by 9am, before the price change. The volume decline lines up with the timing of the price increase and hasn't recovered as of W37 (the brief's own note: "Volume has not come back").

**Bottom line**: the higher price more than offset the higher butter cost per croissant, but you're selling enough fewer croissants that total weekly profit from the category is down about $268, roughly 14%, not up.
